newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT--Philips, Lucent joint venture.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT--Philips, Lucent joint venture.

text.p: Telecommnications company Lucent Technologies Inc. and electronics giant Philips Electronics NV on Tuesday said they agreed to merge their consumer communications products businesses into a jointly owned company valued at $2.5 billion.

The company, called Philips Consumer Communications, will provide corded and cordless phones and answering machines, and develop, manufacture and market a line of products including digital and analog cellular phones, screen phones, and pagers.
A full text of the company's press release follows.
Philips Electronics N.V. and Lucent Technologies Plan Joint Venture to Create World Leader in Consumer Communications Products

MURRAY HILL, N.J., June 17 /PRNewswire/ -- Philips Electronics N.V. (NYSE: PHG) and Lucent Technologies (NYSE: LU) said today they have agreed to merge their consumer communications products businesses into a new company called Philips Consumer Communications, a jointly owned venture of Philips and Lucent. The union of these businesses will create a $2.5 billion company that will be the world's leading provider of corded and cordless phones and answering machines and will have a full range of products in the wireless arena.

The new company will develop, manufacture and market a comprehensive line of products, including digital and analog cellular phones, corded and cordless phones, answering machines, screen phones, and pagers.

The transaction is scheduled to be completed by October 1, 1997, with 60 percent of the venture owned by Philips and 40 percent by Lucent Technologies. The joint venture will be headquartered in New Jersey with regional offices around the world and will be established in the United States.

"This is a highly strategic venture that dramatically advances our growth plans," said Cor Boonstra, president of Philips. "By joining with the number one provider of phones in the U.S., we gain a significant presence in this key market as well as access to the advanced technological capabilities of Bell Labs," he added. "The complementary nature of the two businesses in terms of geographic reach, research and development, distribution and corporate culture is quite extraordinary."

"With advances in technology, the lines between consumer telephony and consumer electronics are blurring," said Lucent Technologies President Rich McGinn. "So it makes strategic sense to join our consumer telephony unit with Philips, a consumer electronics giant with worldwide distribution capabilities and a well-respected global brand."

"Despite the wonderful people, assets and ideas at both Philips and Lucent, neither one can do alone what we can achieve together," said Carly Fiorina, executive vice president of Lucent and president of its Consumer Products business. "This partnership will allow us to serve our customers -- both retail and service providers -- and take better advantage of this huge and growing market." Industry experts say the consumer communications market reached $20 billion in 1996 and is currently growing at 14 percent annually.

Michael McTighe, 43, managing director of Philips Consumer Communications (PCC), will become CEO of the new company. McTighe joined Philips in 1995 to lead its entry into the consumer telephony market. Prior to joining Philips, he was a top executive in Motorola's cellular subscriber division and before that spent 10 years at General Electric.
Carly Fiorina will serve on the board of directors of the new company and will assume another senior management role at Lucent Technologies when the transition is complete.
McTighe emphasized that both companies will move ahead with current product commitments to retailers and service providers. "We see very little duplication in product lines," he added.

"This company will hit the ground running this holiday season, delivering more than 40 new products -- from the industry's longest-range cordless phone to a new analog cellular phone with the longest talk/standby time available," remarked Fiorina.
The companies expect the vast majority of the 8,400 Lucent and the 4,000 Philips employees currently in their consumer telephony businesses will move to the new venture.

"This venture is designed for growth," said the company's new CEO McTighe. "We plan to move ahead with the recently announced expansions of operations by Philips and Lucent in the United States, Mexico and Singapore. And we will continue to invest heavily in promoting the Philips consumer brand, with increased emphasis in the United States as a result of this new joint venture."

Philips is one of the world's largest electronics companies. Its Consumer Communications division designs, manufactures and markets worldwide a comprehensive line of personal communications products, including digital and analog cellular and cordless phones as well as corded phones, pagers, answering machines, and screen phones.

Lucent Technologies builds, manufactures and delivers a wide range of public and private networks, communications systems and software, electronic components and telephones for consumers and businesses. Its Consumer Products unit manufactures, sells services and leases communications products for consumer, small office and home office use, including corded phones, digital and analog cellular and cordless phones, and digital answering systems. Most households in the United States have Lucent-manufactured telephones. SOURCE Lucent Technologies
